name: Afghanistan
summary_text: Afghanistan under the Taliban is the most hostile environment on this map for a transgender person. The 2024 Morality Law (PVPV) obliges the regime's virtue police to prevent "homosexuality" and "lesbianism"; the Taliban applies the death penalty for same-sex relations under its interpretation of Sharia; and documented practice against LGBTIQ people includes beatings, sexual violence in detention, forced confessions, and house-to-house searches. Transgender Afghans report living in hiding, in windowless rooms, for years. There is no legal recognition, no protection, no functioning consular protection, and no tourism infrastructure that would allow a visitor to blend in. A discovered trans visitor would face the same enforcement apparatus as local LGBTIQ people: detention with routine sexual and physical abuse of queer detainees, prosecution for moral crimes, and corporal punishment that UN experts say is escalating into 2026. This is the reference point for the very bottom of the risk scale.

sources.title: 3.17. LGBTIQ persons | European Union Agency for Asylum
sources.claim_summary: European Union Agency for Asylum (EUAA), Country Guidance on Afghanistan 2024, section 3.17 'LGBTIQ persons': assesses LGBTIQ persons as a profile at risk for international-protection purposes under Taliban rule.

sources.title: 4.5. LGBTIQ+ persons | European Union Agency for Asylum
sources.claim_summary: EUAA Country of Origin Information report — Afghanistan Country Focus, section 4.5 'LGBTIQ+ persons': detailed COI on the situation of LGBTIQ+ persons, including punishment under the de facto authorities.

sources.title: “Even If You Go to the Skies, We’ll Find You”: LGBT People in Afghanistan After the Taliban Takeover | HRW
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch / OutRight report 'Even If You Go to the Skies, We'll Find You' (Jan 2022), based on 60 interviews with LGBT Afghans after the Taliban takeover. Documents Taliban members attacking or threatening people because of sexual orientation or gender identity, abuse from family members and neighbours who support the Taliban, people fleeing their homes, and lives built over years disappearing overnight.

sources.title: A Mountain on My Shoulders: 18 Months of Taliban Persecution of LGBTIQ Afghans | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International report 'A Mountain on My Shoulders: 18 Months of Taliban Persecution of LGBTIQ Afghans' (Feb 2023), based on interviews with 22 LGBTIQ Afghans still in the country (Sept-Oct 2022). Finds Taliban security officials pursuing LGBTIQ people - especially gay men and trans women - more systematically than in the first months of rule, with physical and sexual assault, arbitrary detention, and public flogging for alleged same-sex relations confirmed by the Taliban Supreme Court on social media.

sources.title: Afghanistan's LGBTQ in mortal danger under the Taliban
sources.claim_summary: DW report (Oct 2021) profiling 'Danish', a trans man hiding in a windowless back room in Kabul after the Taliban takeover, and his gay friend Khalid. Describes LGBTQ people facing the death penalty under Taliban rule and the only realistic option being to flee the country.

sources.title: Hidden Atrocities: The Unseen Struggle of Afghanistan’s LGBTQ+ Community Under Taliban Rule - report and interview - JURIST - Features - Legal News & Commentary
sources.claim_summary: JURIST feature (Nov 2024) on findings by the Rainbow Organization of Afghanistan, a group of Afghan LGBTQ+ refugees in Bremen. Documents systematic persecution under Taliban rule; notes that even before 2021 no legal framework protected LGBTQ people, and that transgender individuals are especially exposed.

sources.title: DEC12-07312024-15 - Afghanistan Justice Archive
sources.claim_summary: Translation of Article 22 of the Taliban's PVPV (Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice) Law (July 2024) by the Afghanistan Justice Project. The article tasks morality enforcers with preventing a wide range of 'evils' including adultery and related conduct, codifying moral surveillance that reaches LGBTQ+ identity, women's public speech, and cultural expression.

OHCHR press release (Mar 2026): UN human-rights experts condemn the Taliban's surging use of public corporal punishment — at least 1,110 people flogged in 2025 alone, nearly double 2024 — warning women, girls and LGBT+ people face heightened punishment for 'moral crimes' such as adultery, 'illicit relationships' and 'sodomy'.

sources.title: Afghanistan | Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: Human Dignity Trust country profile: Afghanistan criminalises same-sex sexual activity between men and between women, with severe penalties. (Only the opening of the profile was retrievable at fetch time.)

sources.title: LGBTQ Afghans say they face abuse in detention as Taliban crackdown intensifies | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Nov 2024): 'LGBTQ Afghans say they face abuse in detention as Taliban crackdown intensifies' — first-person accounts of arbitrary detention, beatings and sexual abuse in Taliban custody.
